transcript:
Meeting: POC weekly sync - model selection & pinning
Date: 2026-07-28
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Acme Head of ML), Ben Park (Acme Infra), Maya Singh (Acme Security), Alex Chen (Acme PM)

Summary:
- Reviewed recent benchmark runs on candidate models: redwood-vicuna-1.2 (quantized) vs open-v2-13B and vendor-hosted opt-like model.
- Agreement toward pinning redwood-vicuna-1.2 for pilot but with explicit rollback/fallback policy to open-v2-13B if latency > SLA or quality regressions.
- Action items: Redwood to run additional 99th-percentile latency bench, share pinning config syntax and security docs; Customer to provide traffic profile and finalize hosted vs dedicated decision.

Topics:
- Model selection criteria (latency, cost, hallucination rate)
- Version pinning mechanics and how rollbacks/fallbacks work
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: ok hey everyone thanks for joining. uh quick roll call, then we'll jump into the bench results and the pinning plan.
[00:08] Lena: hi hi lena here.
[00:10] Ben: ben on infra.
[00:12] Maya: maya for security.
[00:14] Alex: alex, pm.
[00:16] Diego: diego here from redwood.
[00:18] Samira: great, thanks. so diego I think you had the run summary?
[00:22] Diego: yeah I pulled the runs from yesterday. we ran three primary variants: redwood-vicuna-1.2 quant (that's our quantized profile), open-v2-13b base and vendor-opt-13b-hosted. the key callouts: p50 is fine across all, p95 starts to diverge around 400 tokens and at p99 redwood-vicuna-1.2 quant is 20-30% faster on GCP a2-like instances. throughput also slightly higher due to better batching behavior and prefix cache hit on our runtimes.
[00:45] Lena: can you repeat the p99 numbers? I kind of missed the units.
[00:48] Diego: yeah so rough numbers: open-v2-13b p99 ~ 980 ms, vendor-opt ~ 1.1s, redwood-vicuna-1.2 quant ~ 720-750 ms on the sample prompt set we used. caveat is sequence length distribution is biased toward 350 tokens for our test prompts.
[01:10] Ben: that's great. what's the memory footprint? we've got concerns about GPU mem on our dedi nodes.
[01:15] Diego: the quantized variant is about 14GB resident with KV cache peaks at ~6GB for those sequence lengths. so on a 48GB instance you'd be comfortable with 3 concurrent workers, but if you want more density we can recommend lower batch sizes or a different quant profile.
[01:34] Maya: security question — if we pin a model version, what happens with key management and audit logs? we need to know KMS integration and whether calls show model version in audit trails.
[01:44] Samira: yes good call. redwood private or dedicated integrates with customer KMS; audit logs include model id and version metadata for each call. Diego, correct me if I'm messing up the term — I sometimes say 'model pin' or 'deployment pin'.
[01:58] Diego: yeah both are used. the runtime stores model.version metadata with every request and the control plane logs rollouts. we'll share the audit log sample and the SOC2 artifact that shows logging coverage.
[02:08] Maya: perfect, please include retention windows and whether logs can be forwarded to customer-specified cloud storage.
[02:14] Samira: noted.
[02:16] Alex: question on fallbacks — we saw a note in the docs about automatic fallback to a cheaper model. can you explain the policy?
[02:23] Diego: sure. you can configure routing policies: preference order, thresholds based on latency or errors, or cost-based. for the pilot we recommend primary pin to redwood-vicuna-1.2@v1.2.3 and fallback to open-v2-13b@v1.0.0 if p99 exceeds 1.2s for more than n seconds or error rate crosses 2%. it's configurable and immediate rollback can be triggered manually from console or via API.
[02:52] Lena: do we get per-route metrics? we have multiple prompt templates and want to pin per-route.
[02:58] Diego: yes, per-route and per-model metrics, and you can pin per-route. also we have KV/prefix cache insights so you can see hit rates by prompt template.
[03:08] Ben: earlier you said prefix cache — is that the same as the KV cache? sometimes our infra team calls it the kv-cache and sometimes prefix cache.
[03:15] Diego: yeah sorry, I use them interchangeably. the runtime stores prefix keys in the kv-cache to avoid recomputing, helps latency for repeated prompts.
[03:22] Maya: any gotchas for on-prem/dedicated? e.g., network egress or private control plane?
[03:28] Samira: for dedicated we can do private control plane with peering, or full private (VPC) deployment. for on-prem we support an air-gapped package but some autoscaling features and console UX are limited. Diego can share a matrix of features by deployment mode.
[03:42] Diego: yep I'll attach the matrix — includes what telemetry is forwarded, which features are supported in air-gapped mode, and where the KMS connector sits.
[03:50] Alex: about pinning — what does the pin config look like? is it a yaml? can our infra team manage it in terraform?
[03:58] Diego: it's a small json/yaml snippet. example: route: '/api/chat', primary: 'redwood-vicuna-1.2@v1.2.3', fallback: 'open-v2-13b@v1.0.0', thresholds: { p99_ms: 1200, error_pct: 2 }, rollout: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%. we can export via the API so infra can manage via terraform. sorry that was a bit noisy — the thresholds json we'll send in the notes.
[04:34] Lena: I heard canary, are canaries supported for pinning? we want gradual rollouts to detect quality regressions.
[04:39] Diego: yes canaries and A/B; you can route a percentage of traffic or specific user cohorts. plus automated rollback on metric triggers.
[04:46] Samira: a few more items from the latest evals — we saw some hallucination patterns on prompts with lists, redwood-vicuna performed slightly better on truthfulness scores but open-v2 had fewer token churns. these are small but worth tracking.
[05:00] Lena: do you have the eval spreadsheet link?
[05:03] Samira: yes shared in the chat — "redwood-acme-evals-2026-07-27.xlsx". diego can call out specific tests.
[05:10] Diego: the prompt set for list-heavy tasks shows a 3% lower factual error rate for redwood-vicuna-1.2; however open-v2 produced more concise outputs, so for UX we need to look at length tokens and scoring tradeoffs.
[05:26] Ben: from infra perspective we prefer the model with lower memory footprint if quality delta is small. that pushes us toward open-v2 sometimes. can pinning support rapid rollback with no downtime?
[05:36] Diego: yes, rollbacks are instantaneous at the control-plane routing level; in-flight requests finish on the previous model but new requests route to the rollback target, so effectively negligible downtime.
[05:46] Maya: any encryption-at-rest differences between hosted and ded?
[05:50] Samira: hosted api keeps model artifacts encrypted by our KMS; in dedicated/private we can bring-your-own KMS and ensure keys never leave your VPC. we'll add this to the security doc.
[05:59] Alex: timeline for pilot decision — we want to start the pilot next week if possible. what do you need from us to enable hosted pilot vs dedicated?
[06:07] Samira: for hosted pilot we just need sample traffic, SSO user list and a short PII checklist. for dedicated pilot we need expected concurrency, preferred instance shapes, and a legal/compliance kickoff. hosted is fastest.
[06:21] Lena: can we get a price delta on hosted vs dedicated for our expected 30k req/day?
[06:26] Samira: yes I'll include a breakout in the pricing sheet — we usually show per-token + per-hour reserved capacity numbers for Dedicated.
[06:33] Ben: last infra detail — are there prebuilt terraform modules for pinning config?
[06:37] Diego: yes we have a provider and examples. I'll point you to the repo.
[06:40] Maya: one more compliance ask — we need to know whether model logs include prompt text or just metadata for compliance. can you confirm?
[06:48] Samira: by default we log metadata and model ids; raw prompts are not stored unless you opt-in for debugging. for pilots we can enable redaction and only store hashes. we'll document the retention and redaction options.
[06:59] Alex: ok sounds good. so it sounds like consensus is to pin redwood-vicuna-1.2@v1.2.3 with fallback to open-v2-13b@v1.0.0 and defined thresholds and canary rollout.
[07:10] Lena: yes that's our leaning. Ben and I will confirm infra capacity and come back.
[07:14] Ben: yep.
[07:15] Maya: I'll review the SOC2 and logging details.
[07:18] Samira: great. next steps recap — Samira to send pricing and pilot terms; diego to run the 99th-percentile bench on the pinned model with your sample traffic; ben to send traffic profile; maya to send security questions. we also scheduled an optional dry-run of the rollout next Wednesday — does that work for everyone?
[07:36] Lena: next wednesday works for me.
[07:38] Alex: works.
[07:39] Diego: sounds good. I'll post the bench results and the pin config snippet in git/drive.
[07:45] Samira: any final questions?
[07:48] Lena: none from me. thanks.
[07:50] Ben: thanks.
[07:51] Maya: thank you.
[07:52] Samira: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and artifacts.
